title: The laborer who was Shiva
hook: Shiva hires out as a lazy laborer in Madurai, takes a king's cane, and every being feels the blow
tomorrow: a minister carrying a king's gold meets a teacher under a tree.

segments.voice: Yesterday, a thread of the Shiva Sutras said wonder marks the stages of yoga. Today the same book builds a theater, and a story from Madurai walks onto its stage.
screen: `WONDER MARKS THE WAY.` · `TODAY: A THEATER, AND A LABORER.`

segments.voice: The river Vaigai has burst its banks at Madurai, and the king orders every household to send someone to carry earth to the breach. An old woman named Vandi sells steamed rice cakes, puttu, and every morning she offers the first one to Shiva. She has no son, no husband, no one to send. Then a young laborer turns up at her door. I'll do your share, he says, and you can pay me in puttu. He eats the cakes. And then he doesn't work.
screen: `THE RIVER BREAKS ITS BANKS.` → `AN OLD WOMAN WITH NO ONE TO SEND.` → `A LABORER, PAID IN PUTTU.`

segments.voice: This story comes from the Tamil temple tradition of Madurai, one of Shiva's sacred games. The laborer sings. He dances. He naps under a tree. Every other stretch of the bank rises, and Vandi's stays open. The king comes to inspect, sees the gap and the sleeping laborer, and strikes him across the back with his cane. And the blow lands on everyone. The king feels it on his own back. So does every worker on the bank, every creature in the land. The laborer tips one basket of earth into the breach, the bank closes, and he's gone. Then the king understands whom he struck. Now set it beside the Shiva Sutras, from far-off Kashmir. Nartaka atma: the self is a dancer. The stage is the inner self. The spectators are the senses. Kashmir Shaivism teaches that there is one consciousness, and it is Shiva's, playing every part: the king, the old woman, the laborer, you. That's why one blow could land on everyone. It was always one back. Many teachers read the dancer line as a picture of someone awake: not someone who quits the roles, but someone who plays each one fully and never forgets who's dancing. Shiva played a lazy laborer so well that a king hit him, and never stopped being Shiva. Here's where it meets an ordinary day. You'll play a dozen parts before tonight: student, child, annoyed friend. Play them all the way. And the person across from you, the one you're tempted to strike, is played by the same one.
screen: `SHIVA'S SACRED GAMES, MADURAI.` · `THE BLOW LANDS ON EVERYONE.` · `NARTAKA ATMA: THE SELF IS A DANCER.` · `ONE CONSCIOUSNESS, EVERY PART.` · then, large: `IT WAS ALWAYS ONE BACK.`

segments.voice: Name a few parts you've already played today: the one who got up, the one who answered a message, the one who was short with someone, or kind. Let each one step onto the inner stage, take a bow and step off, and notice the one who's watching, who was there for every part. If you pray, offer the whole performance to Shiva with Om namah shivaya. If you don't, just rest as the one watching.
Nartaka atma. The self is a dancer: in Kashmir Shaivism, one consciousness, Shiva's, playing every part.
Your line: one consciousness plays every part. It was always one back. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1142 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE MINISTER UNDER THE TREE.`
